**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted as the **TARGET — nothing here is built.** The tenancy model is the **owner's** (UD-1 as revised 2026-10-07: *"sebagai konteks tenant adalah perusahaan kalibrator yang melayani faskes"* — "the tenant is the calibration company that serves health facilities"); the mechanism, and the reading that a hospital performing its own calibration stays a valid tenant, are decided by the ADR-writing agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it) and are flagged for the owner's confirmation in `TASKS/BACKLOG.md` Q-57·T · **Card:** P12-02 · **Builds in:** P18-03, P19-04, P20-07, P21-09, P22-09; threat model P17-06; security review P17-07 · **Works with:** ADR-048 (includes are scoped, join type kept), ADR-064 (roles global; unscoped models are reviewed), ADR-073 (hookless statics), ADR-084 (**not amended** — reaffirmed), ADR-085 (socket re-check), ADR-094 (users named in a body), ADR-107 (snapshots), ADR-120 (cache keys per scope) · **Supersedes:** the first reading of UD-1 (facility = tenant, provider staff acting through a per-facility grant and an "active facility" switch), which was **never written as an ADR**: the owner corrected it before this entry existed, so there is no withdrawn ADR to keep · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-upstream-adrs.md` · **Amended by:** Amendment 1 (P18-03, 2026-10-07, below § Status — the bound menu ceiling, the marker list and its refusal rule, `FACILITY_READABLE`, three new slugs); Amendment 2 (P19-04, 2026-10-07 — the entity, columns, migrations, hook mechanics, binding, device moves; below Amendment 1); Amendment 3 (P20-07, 2026-10-08 — built: the database fills `client_facility_id` on insert for today's create paths; below Amendment 2)

**Confirmed by the owner 2026-10-07** (Q-57·T (a)): a tenant is whoever does the calibration work — a calibration company serving many facilities, or a hospital's IPSRS serving itself with exactly one `is_self` facility; existing tenants keep working. Q-57·T (b)–(d) remain working decisions awaiting confirmation. Serial uniqueness (UD-9) decided the same day: per facility, `(tenant_id, client_facility_id, serial_number)`.

### Context

Callibrator's documents describe two kinds of tenant "on opposite sides of the same transaction": healthcare facilities (`HEALTHCARE ADMIN` tenants) and calibration providers (`CALIBRATOR ADMIN` tenants), isolated from each other (`docs/PLAN/00-PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`). Nothing in the code connects the two sides: a user has exactly one `tenantId` (`backend/src/models/user.model.ts`), only the super admin crosses tenants, and ADR-084 §2 settled that no structural relationship (the hierarchy) grants visibility.

The upstream SKP IPM application (`docs/UPSTREAM/00-OVERVIEW.md`) is one provider serving 118 facilities (*faskes*) — hospitals, clinics, community health centres, district health offices — with its own admins and technicians, plus two kinds of facility staff: read-only `client` accounts and facility technicians (`teknisi_client`). It enforced the facility boundary **per controller**, and that is where its worst findings came from (S-04, S-05, S-11: a facility id taken from the URL, query or body).

On 2026-10-07 the coordinator first put UD-1 as "each facility = its own hospital tenant; the provider acts through a revocable cross-tenant grant". The owner then clarified the premise: **the tenant is the calibration company; the facilities are its clients.** That removes the cross-tenant working path entirely, and replaces it with a different, smaller problem: inside one tenant, some users (the facility's own staff) must see only their facility.

Two readings of the owner's sentence were possible: (a) the whole product's tenant becomes the calibration company and hospitals stop being tenants; (b) the tenant is *whoever performs or manages the calibration work*. Reading (a) would invalidate every existing hospital tenant and the hospital-side roles; nothing the owner said asks for that. This ADR takes reading (b) and asks the owner to confirm it (Q-57·T).

### Decision

1. **A tenant is an organisation that performs or manages calibration and maintenance work** — the data controller's processor and the subscriber of the product. Two shapes, one model:
   - **a service company** (e.g. the upstream provider) serving many client facilities;
   - **a facility serving itself** — a hospital whose own maintenance unit (IPSRS) runs its devices. It is a tenant with exactly one client facility: itself.

   Existing tenants stay valid with no change of meaning. Isolation **between** tenants is exactly as today (deny-by-default hooks, 404, ADR-084 unchanged). There is **no cross-tenant working path**: no grant, no membership table, no "act in another tenant" switch.

2. **A health facility (faskes) is a first-class entity inside a tenant: `client_facilities`** (new, tenant-scoped). No existing model fits: `tenants`/`tenant_hierarchies` are tenants (a facility as a child tenant is the rejected cross-tenant shape), `warehouses` are locations (a facility *has* rooms), `vendors` are suppliers.

   | Column | Note |
   |---|---|
   | `id` uuid PK; `tenant_id` NN → tenants RESTRICT | scoped by the hooks like every tenant table |
   | `name`, `code` | `UNIQUE (tenant_id, code)` — per tenant only (no global uniqueness: the oracle trap) |
   | `kind` ENUM | `hospital`, `clinic`, `health_centre`, `district_office`, `laboratory`, `other` |
   | `is_self` boolean NN | the tenant's own premises; **exactly one per tenant** (partial unique `(tenant_id) WHERE is_self`) |
   | `status` ENUM | `active`, `inactive`, `ended` — a client that leaves is `ended`, never deleted; its history stays |
   | address, phone, contact fields; `legacy_id` | the ETL's link (Phase 24) |
   | `UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)` | the target of composite foreign keys |
   | timestamps, `deleted_at`, `is_deleted` | soft delete refused while any facility-scoped row references it (RESTRICT) |

   Every tenant gets its `is_self` facility at migration time and at tenant creation (`tenant.service#createTenant`), so "the tenant's own devices" is always a facility too and the model has no special case for self-served hospitals or for a provider's own reference standards.

3. **Facility-scoped models carry `client_facility_id`**, with a **composite foreign key `(tenant_id, client_facility_id)` → `client_facilities (tenant_id, id)`**, so a row can never name another tenant's facility. A model is facility-scoped **if and only if** it declares the attribute — the same "declare the column and the hooks find you" rule as `tenantId`.
   - **NOT NULL** (the device-anchored evidence chain): `calibration_devices`, `calibration_records`, `certificates`, `maintenance_work_orders` (its `device_id` is NOT NULL), `iot_readings`, and the new `inspection_sessions`, `inspection_results` (ADR-126). The value is the device's facility, stamped from the parent in the service and checked by the composite key; a device moved between facilities is a later, separately audited operation (P19-03) — children keep the facility they were created in.
   - **NULLABLE** (rows that may or may not belong to a facility): `attachments` (a device photo or certificate PDF has its resource's facility; an SOP's has none), `warehouses` (a facility's rooms vs the provider's own stores, UD-10), `non_conformances` (`device_id` nullable), `users` (§ 4).
   - A NULL facility means **provider-internal**: a facility-bound principal never sees it (`client_facility_id = $f` never matches NULL), so the nullable case needs no extra rule.
   - **Every facility-owned row has it NOT NULL** (the DPIA's R-04 (3), `docs/UPSTREAM/06-DPIA.md`, where it is called `faskes_id`): on a nullable table a CHECK ties it to the row's kind — an attachment whose `resource_type` is a facility-scoped resource (a device, a calibration record, an IPM session, a work order) must carry it; a room (`warehouses` of kind room) must carry it. Rows that reference each other inside the chain use composite keys `(tenant_id, client_facility_id, …)` where the spec (P19-04) can make them, so a session cannot name a device of another facility.
   - The exact list is fixed by the P19-04 spec and pinned by a guard (§ 10): a new model joining the evidence chain must declare the attribute or be listed as provider-internal with a reason.

4. **A user is facility-bound if and only if `users.client_facility_id` is set.** Bound-ness is a property of the user row, set by the tenant's administrator, never derived from the role name and never read from a request. Provider staff (and a self-served hospital's own staff) are unbound and see every facility of their tenant.
   - A bound user's facility must be `active`; an `inactive` or `ended` facility refuses its bound users at authentication with 403, as a suspended tenant does (A-101).
   - Bound users may hold only the facility-side roles `HEALTHCARE ADMIN`, `HEALTHCARE TECHNICIAN`, `FACILITY MAINTENANCE`, `ROOM USER` (refused with 400 otherwise, in the service and in the user-create/update contract). Which of them the upstream `client` and `teknisi_client` accounts get is UD-4 (open).
   - `users.email` stays globally unique: a facility employee has one account.

5. **The second scope dimension.** The request context (`tenantContext.middleware.ts`, `TenantContextStore`) gains `clientFacilityId: ClientFacilityId | null` and `facilityBound: boolean`, set by `auth` from the **loaded user row** only — never a header, body or query (the upstream's S-05/S-11 shape is impossible by construction). The tenant dimension is unchanged. The facility dimension is applied by **the same global hooks**, in the same places (root `where`, every include's ON clause with the join type pinned as ADR-048 does, bulk updates/destroys, the wrapped hookless statics of ADR-073, create stamping, `bulkCreate`/`upsert` refusal of a mismatched row), resolved as:

   ```
   options.skipFacilityScope       -> skip   (explicit, greppable; a separate opt-out from skipTenantScope)
   no context                      -> skip   (as for tenants: pre-auth, migrations, schedulers)
   isSystemTask / isSuperAdmin     -> skip
   not facilityBound               -> skip   (provider staff: the tenant predicate alone)
   facilityBound, model facility-scoped
                 and clientFacilityId -> filter client_facility_id = clientFacilityId
   facilityBound, model facility-scoped, no facility -> DENY (NO_FACILITY_UUID)
   facilityBound, model tenant-scoped but NOT facility-scoped
                 and not on FACILITY_READABLE -> DENY (NO_TENANT_UUID: the model is provider-internal)
   ```

   - **The last line is what makes it deny-by-default.** A bound user is not merely filtered on the facility tables: every other tenant table (stock, vendors, QMS, kanban, tickets, billing, settings, other users, audit) answers nothing to them unless it is on a reviewed `FACILITY_READABLE` list with its own reason and its own rule (expected to hold only per-user rows such as the caller's own notifications and sessions, which are already keyed by user). A new tenant model is therefore invisible to facility users until someone decides otherwise.
   - On create, a bound principal's `client_facility_id` is **stamped and forced** to its own facility; an unbound principal must supply it (validated by the composite key; an id from another tenant cannot satisfy it).
   - Global models (the catalogue, ADR-125; roles; menus) are untouched by either dimension.
   - The tenant-scope unit tests and ADR-048's include tests gain the facility twin: every association under a bound context, both join types.

6. **Cross-facility is 404, exactly like cross-tenant.** Another facility's device, session, record, certificate, file or report is indistinguishable from a missing one for a bound user. A permission failure on their **own** facility's data is 403.

7. **Routes are deny-by-default for bound users, as a second layer.** A route is reachable by a bound principal only if it is explicitly marked **facility-accessible** (a marker the route declares, read by a new guard). Everything else answers 403 to them. The marker is refused by the guard on any route gated by `superAdminOnly` or by an `rbac()` tenant-administration level, so a bound `HEALTHCARE ADMIN` (whose `ROLE_LEVELS` entry equals the tenant-admin tier) can never reach the provider's tenant administration — users, roles, settings, SSO, API keys, backups, billing. Two layers on purpose: the hooks stop data leaving; the route layer stops a bound user reaching an action whose side effects are not row reads (an export job, a webhook test, a search across models).

8. **Raw SQL.** `sql()` statements already bind `tenant_id = $n` (P9-07). A statement naming a facility-scoped table must also bind the facility predicate when the context is bound. A helper produces the fragment from the **context**, never from a parameter: unbound → no predicate; bound → `client_facility_id = $n` with the facility id, or `NO_FACILITY_UUID` if the context has none. There is deliberately **no** `($n IS NULL OR …)` form: a NULL that means "everything" is the RLS fail-open of ADR-029 again. `rawSqlTenantPredicate.d05` gains the twin rule (a statement naming a facility-scoped table must mention `client_facility_id`, or be listed as unreachable by bound principals with a reason).

9. **Everything that is not a query:**
   - **Caches** (ADR-120 dashboard aggregates, permission loads): a key in facility-scoped territory includes the facility id for bound principals (`…:<tenant>:f:<facility>`), never shared with the unbound scope.
   - **Socket.IO** (ADR-031/085): a bound socket joins `facility_<tenantId>_<facilityId>` and its user room, **never** `tenant_<id>`. Every emitter of a facility-scoped event emits to the tenant room (provider staff) and to that facility's room. A guard checks that no bound socket joins a tenant room; the 60-second re-check also re-reads the user's facility and its status.
   - **Reports, exports, PDFs.** By the owner's rule of 2026-10-07 (certificates **and** data exports are rendered in the frontend; no certificate or export file is stored — ADR-095 §4 extended, see ADR-126 § 8), a report or export is a set of **paginated API reads** that the browser renders. Its scoping is therefore the scoping of those reads: the hooks, the route marker, the two-facility tests — there is no export file and no export worker to scope. Any batch job that still runs (none is planned for this phase) carries the facility context into the worker (`jobContext`). Initially facility-accessible: the reads behind the facility's inventory list/export, its IPM reports, its certificates and its devices' attachments — each with a two-facility test.
   - **Search and RAG** (`document_chunks`) are **not** facility-accessible until their own review: one missed branch in a many-table search is a leak.
   - **Storage keys carry the facility:** a facility-owned file is stored at `t/<tenant>/f/<facility>/attachments/<uuid>.<ext>` (derivatives beside it), as `docs/UPSTREAM/08-FILE-POLICY.md` § 7 specifies; provider-internal files keep `t/<tenant>/…`. The key is never the authorisation: **before any signed download URL is issued** the attachment row is loaded **in the caller's context** (both dimensions applied by the hooks — a bound user cannot load another facility's row, so the answer is 404) and the key's facility segment is compared with the row's `client_facility_id`; a mismatch is refused and logged as an integrity error. The code change belongs to Phase 21 (the P8-01 key layout gains the segment); the existing `t/<tenant>/attachments/…` keys of today's tenants stay valid as their self facility's files.
   - **Breach scoping per facility:** `audit_logs.client_facility_id` lets a breach be scoped facility by facility, so each facility — the controller of its records — is told only about its own (DPIA § 8). The notice duty under UU PDP Art. 46 (3 × 24 hours, to the data subjects and the agency) is added to `docs/SECURITY/12-INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md` beside GDPR's 72 hours.
   - **Audit:** `audit_logs` gains a nullable `client_facility_id`, stamped from the row or the context, so a facility view of the trail is possible later; facility users do not read the audit log in this ADR (the audit route is not facility-accessible).
   - **Notifications/reminders** about a facility's devices go to that facility's bound users who hold the menu, and to provider staff — never to another facility's users.
   - **Certificates** (ADR-107): the **customer** printed on a certificate (ISO/IEC 17025 7.8.2) is the client facility, snapshotted at signing; the laboratory is the tenant. For a self-served tenant both are the same organisation.
   - **API keys** stay tenant-wide (unbound). A facility-bound key is not offered; the per-tenant import key (P24-04) is unbound.
   - **SSO/SCIM:** bound users authenticate through the tenant's configuration; a facility cannot bring its own IdP for its staff (one tenant, one SSO configuration) — later decision if asked.
   - **Impersonation:** an operator impersonating a bound user gets that user's bound context — what the user sees is what support sees. No change to the mechanism.
   - **Suspension:** a suspended tenant refuses all its users, bound ones included (unchanged); an `inactive`/`ended` facility refuses only its bound users (§ 4).
   - **Quota and billing:** bound users are users of the tenant and count against `limitSeats` today. Whether facility accounts should count is commercial (Q-57·T asks).

10. **Tests and guards that make it stay true (built with P20-07/P21-09):**
    - `fixtures/twoFacilitySuite.ts` over `memoryDb` (the real models and the real hooks): one tenant, facilities F1 and F2, a bound user in F1, an unbound technician; every facility-accessible `:id` route asserts **404** for F2's row and that F2 is absent from every list, marked `@two-facility <route file> <METHOD> <path>`.
    - `twoFacilityRoutes.guard` (the twin of `twoTenantRoutes.guard`): every facility-accessible `:id` route has a two-facility test.
    - `facilityAccessibleRoutes.guard`: the marker never sits on a platform or tenant-admin route; the list of marked routes is reviewed like `routeGateExemptions`.
    - `facilityScopedModels.guard`: every model on the evidence chain declares `clientFacilityId`, every other tenant model is either provider-internal or on `FACILITY_READABLE` with a reason (the `unscopedModels.d17` pattern).
    - The deny branch: a bound principal with no resolvable facility sees zero rows of every facility-scoped model, and zero rows of every provider-internal model.
    - The A-90 trap: every include of `User` from a facility-scoped model is `required: false` (provider technicians are invisible to bound users), and the author is shown from a snapshot (`performer_snapshot`, ADR-126) — an INNER include would make the facility's own records disappear for its own staff.
    - Socket isolation and cache-key tests for a bound principal.
    - **Coverage the DPIA's R-04 (2) asks for:** the two-facility cases are not only `:id` routes — every list, every export read (ADR-126 § 8), every include tree reachable from a facility-accessible route, every raw-SQL statement naming a facility-scoped table, every socket room and every signed-URL issuance gets a case where a user of facility A asks for facility B's data and gets 404 / nothing / an export containing only A.
    - **No facility-bound user is invited** in any tenant before these guards and suites are green and named in a record, and P17-06/07 have threat-modelled and tested the scope (DPIA R-04 (5)). A bound user never gets a "switch facility" (R-04 (6)): a person who works for two facilities has two accounts, or is provider staff.

11. **Rollout.** Migrations (P20-07): `client_facilities`; one `is_self` facility per existing tenant; `client_facility_id` on the models of § 3, backfilled to the tenant's self facility, then NOT NULL where § 3 says; the composite keys; `users.client_facility_id`; `audit_logs.client_facility_id`. Every existing row lands in a self facility and every existing user stays unbound, so **no current tenant's behaviour changes** until a second facility or a bound user exists. The upstream import (Phase 24) creates **one** provider tenant with 118 client facilities (+ its self facility); the facility users are bound. No bound user is created in any tenant before the two-facility guard and suite are green and P17-07 has reviewed them.

### Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Facility = tenant, provider staff act through a revocable cross-tenant grant with an "active facility" switch** (the first reading of UD-1; 04 § 3 option A) | the owner's correction: the facility is the provider's client, not a subscriber. It also built the first cross-tenant working path (auth, session, socket, audit in two tenants, 118 tenants to onboard) to solve a problem the real model does not have |
| **Facilities as child tenants under the provider** (`tenants.parent_id`) | ADR-084 §2: the hierarchy grants no visibility, so provider staff could not see their clients' devices without the cross-tenant path above |
| **A facility filter in each controller/service** (the upstream's way; 04 § 3 option B as first written) | "remember the WHERE" — the exact mechanism behind upstream S-05/S-11 and behind PR-1; one missed filter leaks a facility's devices to another |
| **Bound-ness from the role** (`ROOM USER` ⇒ bound) | a self-served hospital's own `HEALTHCARE ADMIN` is unbound; a provider's facility admin is bound — same role, different scope. Deriving scope from a role name is also the A-07/N-01 class of bug |
| **Filter only the facility tables; let bound users see the rest of the tenant** | a facility user would read the provider's vendors, stock, kanban, tickets, other clients' names in any table that mentions them; deny-by-default must apply to the whole tenant, not only to the tables we remembered |
| **PostgreSQL RLS for the facility dimension** | rejected for tenants in ADR-029/039 (fail-open `''`, per-request round trips); one mechanism for both dimensions is easier to reason about and test |
| **A `($facility IS NULL OR client_facility_id = $facility)` predicate** | a NULL that means "all" is fail-open; unbound principals get no predicate at all instead |
| **Per-technician facility assignment for provider staff** (a technician sees only assigned facilities) | the owner said provider staff work across their tenant's facilities; addable later as a narrowing set on unbound users without changing this design |
| **Reading (a): the tenant is always a calibration company; hospitals stop being tenants** | invalidates every existing hospital tenant and the hospital-side tenant administration for no stated need; reading (b) contains (a) as its main case |

### Implications, including the bad ones

- **The product description changes.** "Healthcare facilities and calibration providers are two kinds of tenant on opposite sides of the transaction" becomes "a tenant is whoever performs the work; facilities are its clients (or itself)". `docs/PLAN/00`, `PLAN/03`, `PLAN/10`, `SECURITY/05`, `MULTI-TENANCY/README`, `DATABASE/00` are amended with this ADR, as target.
- **A hospital with its own IPSRS that also uses an outside provider has two copies of its world**: its own tenant, and a client record inside the provider's tenant. Nothing flows between them (no cross-tenant path, by design). Moving records between them is export/import, a later decision (Q-57·T).
- **A second dimension in the most security-critical code in the system.** `tenantScope.util.ts` grows a second resolution order; every hook, the include walk, the static wrappers and the create stamp gain a twin branch. The tests double. This is the code ADR-048 found wrong once; it must be reviewed as such (P17-07).
- **The `FACILITY_READABLE` deny is strict.** Features a facility user might reasonably expect — their own profile pieces stored in tenant tables, a ticket to the provider, a notification preference — fail closed until each is reviewed onto the list. That is the price of the default.
- **A bound `HEALTHCARE ADMIN` is not a tenant administrator.** The role's level says it is; the route marker and the guard override that for bound users. Anyone who later adds a tenant-admin route and marks it facility-accessible "for the facility admin" is refused by the guard — and needs an ADR.
- **The A-90 trap widens.** Provider staff are invisible to bound users, so every author column on the evidence chain needs `required: false` plus a snapshot, and every existing list a facility user can reach must be swept (P19-04).
- **Backfill on every existing table of § 3.** One migration touches the largest tables (`calibration_records`, `attachments`); it runs in one transaction per table and is proved with `upgradeBoot.am3.live` on production-shaped data. Indexes on the new column live in the migration (ADR-100 Am. 3).
- **Moving a device between facilities** has no answer yet: its history stays in the old facility (children keep their facility). P19-03 decides.
- **Seats:** facility accounts count as tenant seats until the owner decides otherwise.
- **Faskes groupings** (a district office over its health centres, UD-10) are not modelled: a bound user sees exactly one facility. A group view is a later, explicit decision.

### Security analysis

| Threat | Control |
|---|---|
| Bound user names another facility's id in a path, body or query | the facility comes from the user row only; the hooks filter every read and include; the answer is 404 identical to missing (§ 5, § 6) |
| Bound user reads a provider-internal table (vendors, stock, other users, audit) | the DENY branch for tenant models not facility-scoped (§ 5) and the route layer (§ 7) |
| Bound facility admin escalates to tenant administration | the route marker is refused on tenant-admin and platform routes by guard (§ 7) |
| A new table or route forgets the facility | the model guard and the route default (deny) make forgetting fail closed; the two-facility guard makes a marked route without a test fail the build (§ 10) |
| Raw SQL bypasses the hooks | context-derived predicate helper, no NULL-means-all form, d05 twin rule (§ 8) |
| Cache, socket room or batch job carries another facility's data | facility in the key; bound sockets never join the tenant room; job context bound (§ 9) |
| A signed URL or a guessed storage key reaches another facility's file | keys carry the facility segment; a URL is issued only after the row is loaded in the caller's context and its facility matches the key (§ 9) |
| Cross-tenant | unchanged — the tenant dimension is untouched and still applies first |
| Cross-facility existence oracle through a uniqueness 409 | any value a **bound** user can write is unique **per facility** (`(tenant_id, client_facility_id, …)` — e.g. the serial, UD-9 / P19-03), so their 409 can only name their own facility's rows; values only provider staff write (facility `code`, the provider-issued QR) stay unique per tenant, and bound users never see them for other facilities |
| Repudiation | audit rows carry the facility; performer snapshots on records |

### Status

**Accepted 2026-10-07 as the target. Not built.** Reading (b) (§ 1: a self-served hospital remains a tenant) awaits the owner's confirmation (Q-57·T); until confirmed it is the working decision. `docs/` amended as target: `PLAN/00-PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`, `PLAN/03-USER-ROLES.md`, `PLAN/10-TENANCY-AND-ONBOARDING.md`, `SECURITY/05-MULTI-TENANCY-SECURITY.md`, `MULTI-TENANCY/README.md`, `DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md`, `SECURITY/12-INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md` (UU PDP notice), `UPSTREAM/00-OVERVIEW.md` § 10, `UPSTREAM/04-SCHEMA-MAPPING.md` § 3/§ 6/§ 9, `UPSTREAM/05-DATA-MIGRATION.md` § 6.1/§ 10, `UPSTREAM/02-FEATURES.md` § B. Mitigations (1)–(4) and (6) of the DPIA's R-04 are specified here (§ 5, § 3, § 10, § 9); (5) is P17-06/07.

### ADR-124 Amendment 1 (2026-10-07, P18-03): the bound menu ceiling in the effective permission; the marker is one reviewed list with a widened refusal rule; `FACILITY_READABLE` and the reviewed service-internal reads; a bound facility admin is read-only; three new slugs, no new role

**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted as the **TARGET — nothing here is built.** Decided by the P18-03 agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it); the cells that wait on an owner decision are marked in the spec (UD-4 (a)–(c), UD-10, UD-17) · **Card:** P18-03 · **Spec:** [`MEMORY/specs/P18-03-facility-scope-permissions.md`](./specs/P18-03-facility-scope-permissions.md) · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-p18-03-role-mapping.md` · **Threat model:** `docs/SECURITY/15-FASKES-SCOPE-THREAT-MODEL.md` AM-8, AM-11, AM-14, OQ-2, OQ-8, OQ-9 (answered here)

**Why an amendment.** ADR-124 § 7 put the route marker between a bound user and the provider's administration, but left the **menu** alone: under ADR-102 the sidebar, the page buttons and `dynamicAccess` read one effective permission, and a bound `HEALTHCARE ADMIN` keeps its role's grants (`users`, `api-keys`, `storage` write …). Its sidebar would show pages whose routes all 403 — the defect ADR-102 removed — and a per-user override could widen it further. ADR-124 § 7's refusal rule also named only `superAdminOnly` and `rbac()`, while tenant backups are `abac`-gated and most administration is slug-gated (threat model FT-37, F-7). The threat model's proposed widening (AM-11) also refused `denyPlatformAuthoring`, which is a Part 11 authorship guard (ADR-052) that the bound technician's own IPM capture will carry.

**Decision.**
1. **The bound menu ceiling.** For a bound principal, `effectivePermission.service` takes, after the role matrix and the per-user override, the minimum with `BOUND_MENU_CEILING[role][slug]` (absent ⇒ none). API, sidebar and buttons therefore agree for bound users with no second rule, and no override lifts a bound user above it. Unbound principals are untouched. The ceiling (spec § 5): every bound role reads `home`, `dashboard`, `equipment`, `calibration`, `certificate`, `maintenance`, `ipm`, `ipm-templates`, writes its own `profile-page`/`change-password`; `HEALTHCARE TECHNICIAN` may also write `calibration` (device registration, only if its role is granted it — UD-4 (b)) and `ipm` (capture); `esignature` waits on UD-17, `warehouse` on UD-10; nothing else. The ceiling never adds a grant.
2. **A bound `HEALTHCARE ADMIN` is read-only in this group** — parity with the upstream `client` account and least privilege. Facility user management by a bound admin is UD-4 (c), recommended not in this group.
3. **The marker is one reviewed constant** (`FACILITY_ACCESSIBLE_ROUTES`, keyed like `routeGateExemptions`, with `kind`, `reason`, optional `selfParam` and `boundGate`) read by one middleware after `auth` that answers 403 to a bound principal on any other route before parameters are read. The exact identifiers are P19-04's.
4. **The guard refuses a marker** on: `superAdminOnly`; `rbac`/`checkRoleLevel` at the tenant-admin tier or above; `abac([TENANT_PERMISSIONS.*])`; a `dynamicAccess` slug on the administrative deny-list held in the guard file (users, roles, permissions, menu groups, sessions administration, tenants and their hierarchy/lifecycle, client facilities, access requests, security, OIDC, WebAuthn administration, network security, SCIM, GDPR administration, custom domains, API keys, webhooks, storage, feature flags, billing, finance, metered billing, audit, data retention, batch jobs, content, notification broadcast); any `certificate` action but `read`; an action outside the union of the bound ceilings; a `public` route. **`denyPlatformAuthoring` is not a criterion** (AM-11 refined). A test (G-P3) ties every ceiling write to a marked route and every marked route to the ceiling.
5. **`FACILITY_READABLE`** holds only context-predicated entries: `ClientFacility` (`id` = own facility, AM-8), `Session`, `Notification`, `ConsentRecord`, `DsarRequest` (each `user_id` = self), and the signature records only once UD-17 marks signing. Infrastructure reads made on a bound user's behalf — tenant settings (time zone, IPM interval, storage), the KMS key, quotas, the subject's own rows for a GDPR export — are **not** listed (that would make them readable by any marked route); they use a reviewed `skipFacilityScope` (G-13 list), never `skipTenantScope`.
6. **Attachment upload** (`POST /attachments`, gated today on `equipment` *read* and accepting `generic`/`ticket`/`post`) is marked for bound principals only with a `boundGate`: an own-facility device or IPM resource loaded in context, and write on its slug.
7. **Three new slugs, no new role, `ROLE_LEVELS` unchanged:** `ipm` and `ipm-templates` under `equipment` (its read reaches them one level down; its write — the level-8 admins — reaches proposal write, as P19-01 asked), `client-facilities` under `mgmt-organization`. `ipm` write is granted explicitly to `TECHNICIAN`, `HEALTHCARE TECHNICIAN` and `FACILITY MAINTENANCE` (a new slug: nothing changes for today's tenants). Whether the technical roles get `calibration` write (device registration, calibration-date entry — UI research 03 F4) is **not** decided here: it widens every tenant's grants, so it is UD-4 (b), open with a recommendation (yes).
8. **`GET /menu-groups/my-permissions`** gains `facilityBound`; a page hides a write action whose route is unmarked for a bound user. The bound user's own facility is read through a self route `GET /client-facilities/mine`.
9. **Threat-model questions answered:** OQ-2 — bound technicians create and edit devices in their facility (subject to UD-4 (b)); the QR is not settable by them, or its 409 names nothing (P19-03 finalises). OQ-8 — the dashboard is facility-accessible only once its two-facility test and the per-facility cache key (G-20) are green; until then the bound home page is built from marked reads. OQ-9 — the per-user tables are on `FACILITY_READABLE`; tickets to the provider are later.

**Alternatives considered.**
| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Rely on the route marker alone; leave the menu as the role grants it | the sidebar and buttons would offer bound users every administrative page their role holds, each 403ing — the ADR-102 defect, re-opened for exactly the users least able to explain it |
| Separate facility-side roles (`FACILITY ADMIN (BOUND)` …) with their own grants | four more roles in `ROLE_LEVELS`, the seed, every role picker and every gate test; and ADR-124 rejected deriving scope from role names — the same role must stay usable unbound in a self-served hospital |
| Lower a bound `HEALTHCARE ADMIN`'s level below 8 at authentication | changes `rbac` comparisons for one principal in a way no gate test sees; level orders escalation, not scope (`docs/PLAN/03`) |
| Put settings, quotas and KMS reads on `FACILITY_READABLE` | makes them readable through any marked route's includes or queries; a per-call reviewed opt-out is narrower |
| A marker tag on each route instead of one list | a tag can be dropped or copied with a route silently; one list is diffed and reviewed like `routeGateExemptions` |
| Refuse the marker on `denyPlatformAuthoring` (AM-11 as proposed) | forbids the upstream facility technician's IPM capture, which carries it; the certificate-action and ceiling rules cover the laboratory-issuance routes it aimed at |
| Grant `calibration` write to the technical roles here | widens every existing tenant's technicians (device delete included) — an owner-visible change, carried as UD-4 (b) |

**Implications, including the bad ones.**
- The effective-permission function — read on every gated request — gains a branch; a defect there could cap an unbound principal. G-P1 runs every seeded role unbound against the unchanged ADR-102 suites.
- Three lists must stay consistent (ceiling, marker list, guard deny-list); G-P3 and G-09 enforce it, but every new facility feature now edits two constants and a test.
- A bound facility admin can do less than its upstream counterpart expects of the word "admin" (nothing it did upstream is lost: `client` was read-only).
- Until UD-4 (b) is answered, a bound facility technician cannot register a device, and the provider's technicians cannot either — the upstream's commonest write waits on an owner decision.
- Reviewed `skipFacilityScope` calls are new opt-outs in services; each is a place the facility hooks do nothing, held only by review (G-13).

**`docs/` amended (as target):** `PLAN/03-USER-ROLES.md` (bound ceiling, new slugs), `SECURITY/05-MULTI-TENANCY-SECURITY.md` (the ceiling and the refusal rule), `UPSTREAM/01-MODULES.md` (§ Role Mapping rewritten to ADR-124; M03 gap), `TASKS/PHASE-12-…` § 3 (UD-4 (b), (c)) and the group DoD gate list (`client-facilities`). `docs/SECURITY/15` (owned by its author) should note the AM-11 refinement — listed in the record.

### ADR-124 Amendment 2 (2026-10-07, P19-04): the client-facility entity as specified — unbound creates default to the self facility; a moved device's children follow it; no soft delete of facilities; one binding operation that revokes sessions; people shown by snapshot or a redacting projection; the route gate over an ordered route index

**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted as the **TARGET — nothing here is built.** Decided by the P19-04 spec agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it); UD-18 (b) (what a leaving facility receives, retention after `ended`) is put to the owner, OQ-3 still awaits the owner · **Card:** P19-04 · **Spec:** [`MEMORY/specs/P19-04-client-facilities.md`](./specs/P19-04-client-facilities.md) (gaps G-F1 … G-F12, § 2) · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-p19-04-client-facilities-spec.md` · **Threat model:** `docs/SECURITY/15` AM-1 … AM-9, AM-12 … AM-15, AM-17 … AM-22 adopted (spec § 18); OQ-1, OQ-5, OQ-12 answered

**Why an amendment.** Writing the entity, the migrations and the hook mechanics against the code found that ADR-124 as written would break or contradict itself in places: it asked unbound principals to supply a facility every existing create path omits; it kept a moved device's children in the old facility while asking for composite keys from every child to `(tenant, facility, device)`; it gave `client_facilities` a soft delete that RESTRICT never stops and whose `defaultScope` would make every include of a facility an INNER JOIN (A-75); it asked a room CHECK on a table with no kind; it showed authors "from a snapshot" that `calibration_records` cannot back-fill (append-only, 0057); and its key-segment check would refuse every file of a moved device and every file of today's tenants.

**Decision.**
1. **Creates (G-F1).** An unbound principal's device create without a facility gets the tenant's **self** facility, in the service; children always take their parent's; bound principals are stamped and forced by the hooks.
2. **Moves (G-F2; OQ-5, OQ-12).** A device's children **follow it**: `POST /calibration-devices/:id/move` (unbound tenant administrator, reason), one transaction inserting a `client_facility_moves` row, naming it in the transaction-local setting `callibrator.facility_move` (the 0089 precedent), updating the device so the composite FKs **`ON UPDATE CASCADE`** carry every child along one path (the certificate → record link is a deferred NO ACTION FK), the append-only triggers (0057's function replaced; P20-05's to match) admitting exactly that change under that setting, the attachments updated and flagged for re-keying, and **two audit rows** (out of the old facility, into the new). Refused (409) into a non-active facility, for a retired device, while an IPM draft is open or a certificate of the device is unsigned, or when the serial exists in the target. Audit rows never move.
3. **Lifecycle (G-F3, G-F11).** `client_facilities` is **not paranoid and has no `defaultScope`**; `ended` is its end of life (`ended → active` only by a tenant administrator with a reason); a hard delete only of a non-self facility nothing references. `inactive`: bound users refused, provider staff work as normal. `ended`: bound users refused, provider staff read only, no new rows (service 409 and a `facility_accepts_inserts` trigger; IoT telemetry dropped by the ingestion service instead). Leaving `active` revokes the bound users' sessions.
4. **Self facility.** Created for **every** tenant (PLATFORM included) by an explicit, audited `createSelfFacility` in every creation path (`createTenant`, child tenants, seeds; the back-fill under the new system actor `system:client-facility-backfill`), proved by a source guard and a live test; always `active` (CHECK); `is_self` and `tenant_id` immutable (trigger). A database trigger that inserted it was rejected (invisible to `memoryDb`, unaudited, a second mechanism).
5. **Columns.** As ADR-124 § 3, plus: `warehouses.client_facility_id` without its CHECK until UD-10 gives warehouses a room kind (G-F4); `audit_logs.client_facility_id` with **no FK and no back-fill** (append-only; a NULL on a pre-migration row means the self facility) and stamped by the audit service from the resource when a caller omits it; `non_conformances` CHECK `(device_id IS NULL) = (client_facility_id IS NULL)`; `attachments` tied to its resource by two **deferred constraint triggers** (AM-7, both sides); the facility column immutable outside the move and the binding by hooks **and** triggers for every role (AM-6); the per-facility serial (UD-9) and `calibration_devices UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)` built in P20-07 (G-F8).
6. **Binding (AM-1, AM-3, AM-14, AM-15; OQ-1).** `PUT /users/:userId/client-facility`, by an unbound tenant administrator, never on oneself, never to the self facility, the bound role set enforced (400) and also by a `users_bound_role_check` trigger, **unbinding names the role explicitly**, the column changeable only under `callibrator.facility_binding`; the user's sessions revoked in the transaction; one audit row per affected facility. JIT/SCIM users of a multi-facility tenant get a `facility_binding_pending` flag (refused with `FACILITY_BINDING_PENDING`), not `INACTIVE` (G-F6). A boot flag `FACILITY_BINDING_ENABLED` (default off) holds the pre-invitation gate.
7. **People (G-F5).** Authors are shown through additive `…Display` fields (`name`, `role`, `organisation`, `redacted`): from a stored snapshot where one exists (ADR-126, ADR-107), else from one batched `users` read through a reviewed `skipFacilityScope`; a bound viewer sees an author bound to **another** facility redacted. No snapshot column is added to `calibration_records`.
8. **Context and route gate (AM-2, AM-12).** The context gains `userId`, `clientFacilityId`, `facilityBound` from the loaded row only, with one writer per entry path; account refusals carry the codes `FACILITY_BINDING_PENDING`, `FACILITY_UNRESOLVED`, `FACILITY_INACTIVE`, `FACILITY_ENDED`. The marker gate runs **from `tenantContextMiddleware`** (33 routers mount `auth` with `router.use`, where `req.route` is unset) over an **ordered route index** built at boot by the walker the guards already use, so it resolves the route Express will dispatch (shadowing included), answering 403 `FACILITY_ROUTE_REFUSED` before any parameter is read.
9. **Storage and links (G-F7, AM-22).** Keys carry the facility from upload; a segment-less (today's) key is valid for the self facility; a move flags `rekey_pending` and a job re-keys copy-then-switch. The attachment-link token (A-365's v2) becomes v3, binding the facility; redemption also requires the row's facility unchanged and a bound issuer still bound there.
10. **Identifiers.** `constants/facilityAccess.ts` (`FACILITY_BOUND_ROLES`, `FACILITY_ACCESSIBLE_ROUTES`, `FACILITY_READABLE` with a per-model attribute — `Session` is `user_id` —, `FACILITY_SCOPE_SKIPS`), `utils/facilityPredicate.util.ts#facilityClause(column, position)` (no facility parameter), `NO_FACILITY_ID` and `ClientFacilityId` in `types/ids.ts`, `dashboard:metrics:v2` keys with `:all` / `:f:<id>`, `emitForRow`, `recipientsFor`, `runForTenant(…, { clientFacilityId })`.
11. **`client-facilities` write is not limited to the self facility by role** (G-F9): that would derive a capability from a role name.
12. **Rollout.** Seven migrations, one transaction per large table, set-based back-fill with `lock_timeout`; this release deploys with `Recreate` (no old replica inserting without a facility).

**Alternatives considered.**
| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Keep children in the old facility on a move (ADR-124 as written) | contradicts the composite keys it asks for; the facility that gave the device up keeps reading its history and the holder gets none |
| Close the old device and open a linked new one in the target facility (OQ-5 option) | the new facility sees no calibration status or history; the QR and serial must be released from a record that still exists; two devices for one instrument |
| FK `(tenant, device)` + a trigger comparing facilities at child insert only (OQ-5 option) | nothing would keep children and device equal after any later write path; the database would no longer prove the invariant the ETL relies on |
| Soft-delete facilities (ADR-124 § 2) | RESTRICT does not stop it; a `defaultScope` hides every device of a deleted facility from includes (A-75) |
| A trigger that creates the self facility | invisible to `memoryDb`, unaudited, a second mechanism beside the service |
| Back-fill a performer snapshot onto `calibration_records` | needs the append-only trigger disabled; records today's names as if they were then |
| Overload `INACTIVE` for JIT/SCIM pending users | hides why an account is refused and collides with an administrator's deactivation |
| Check the route marker in each permission gate | exempted (self/service/inline) routes have no gate, so bound users would pass them |
| Match request paths against the marked patterns only | a shadowing route (`/stats` before `/:id`) would be let through as the marked one |
| A database default (trigger) of a child's facility from its parent | invisible to `memoryDb`; a silent re-ownership instead of a refusal |

**Implications, including the bad ones.**
- A device move rewrites the access attribute of append-only evidence; the exception is narrow (one column, one move row, one transaction) but it is an exception to ADR-062's "every other column immutable", and every future append-only trigger on a facility table must carry it.
- A bound user of the new facility sees records made by another facility's staff (names redacted); the old facility loses sight of the device's history it once saw.
- Seven migrations and a **Recreate** deploy for this release; rollback after the device migration is the backup.
- The route gate depends on replicating Express's matching order; the parity test is the only thing that keeps it true.
- Re-keying after a move copies objects; until the job runs, the integrity check relies on a flag.
- Every response with a person reference grows a `…Display` field (additive; `openapi:breaking` stays green).
- An ended facility's data stays until the retention question (UD-18 (b)) is answered.

**`docs/` amended (as target):** `DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md` (ADR-124 bullet), `SECURITY/05-MULTI-TENANCY-SECURITY.md` (facility section), `UPSTREAM/04-SCHEMA-MAPPING.md` § 4.2 (`id_client`), § 4.6 (keys), `UPSTREAM/05-DATA-MIGRATION.md` § 3.1 (order), § 4 (`id_map.client_facility_id`, AM-28; quarantine reason, AM-27), `TASKS/PHASE-12-…` § 3 (UD-18 (b)). `docs/SECURITY/15` (owned by its author, being edited) should record OQ-1 / OQ-5 / OQ-12 as answered here — listed in the record.

### ADR-124 Amendment 3 (2026-10-08, P20-07): the database fills `client_facility_id` on insert for today's create paths — the self facility for a device while the tenant has no other facility, the device's (or record's) facility for every child; the models declare the column nullable; the as-built choices of the seven migrations

**Date:** 2026-10-08 · **Status:** Accepted, **built** (migrations 0117 – 0123). Decided by the P20-07 implementing agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it) · **Card:** P20-07 · **Spec:** [`MEMORY/specs/P19-04-client-facilities.md`](./specs/P19-04-client-facilities.md) § 5.4, § 6.3 (amended) · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-08-p20-07-client-facilities.md`

**Why an amendment.** Am. 2 § 1 (G-F1) puts the default — "an unbound create without a facility gets the tenant's self facility" — **in the service**, and its alternatives table rejects "a database default (trigger) of a child's facility from its parent". But the services that would supply it are **P21-09's**, and P20-07 makes the column **NOT NULL** first. Built as specified, every existing create path breaks the day 0118 – 0123 deploy: the device, record, certificate, work-order and NC services, IoT ingestion, attachment upload, the bulk import, the scheduler's work orders and the demo seed all write rows without a facility. That is the regression ADR-124 § 11 promised would not happen (G-31: "the self-served hospital must notice nothing"). The spec gave the migration card no instrument for it, so this card decided.

**Decision.**
1. **A BEFORE INSERT trigger fills a missing facility** (`facility_insert_default`, migration 0117; attached by 0118 – 0123, ENABLE ALWAYS). It fills only a NULL, and it never replaces a value the caller gave (the composite key checks that value):
   - **a device** gets its tenant's self facility, **but only while the tenant has no other facility**. A tenant that serves client facilities must name one, or the insert is refused with **23502**. A tenant with no self facility is refused too (23502, with a hint naming `createSelfFacility`);
   - **a record, certificate, work order or IoT reading** gets its device's facility, looked up in the row's own tenant;
   - **a non-conformance** gets its device's facility, and NULL without a device. Clearing the device link also clears the facility, so the CHECK `(device_id IS NULL) = (client_facility_id IS NULL)` holds through 0037's `ON DELETE SET NULL`;
   - **an attachment** linked to a facility-scoped record gets that record's facility, soft-deleted records included. This also applies when a standalone file is linked later (`UPDATE OF resource_type, resource_id`).
2. **The models declare `clientFacilityId` with `allowNull: true`** (typed `CreationOptional<ClientFacilityId>`), and the database holds NOT NULL. Sequelize's own notNull check would otherwise refuse a create that omits it before the trigger runs. On a fresh install `db.sync()` builds the column nullable, and 0118 – 0122 set NOT NULL (spec § 6.3 said sync would build it NOT NULL). `facilityScopedModels.guard` holds `allowNull: true` and no `references` or index on every facility-scoped model.
3. **The service default stays the target.** P21-09 makes the unbound create supply the facility explicitly (Am. 2 § 1); the trigger then remains a backstop. P21-09 decides whether to keep the device branch once every writer names a facility, and records that decision. The child branches stay: they can only produce the one value the composite key accepts.
4. **As-built choices of the seven migrations**, so the next reader does not re-derive them:
   - The children's composite keys copy `ON DELETE` from 0037's single-column `device_id` keys: records, certificates and readings are RESTRICT; work orders are CASCADE; non-conformances are `SET NULL (client_facility_id, device_id)`. Two keys on one column must not disagree when a device row is deleted.
   - 0119 lifts 0057's append-only trigger for its back-fill only, as DDL inside the migration's transaction, then restores and asserts its exact state.
   - A linked attachment whose record no longer exists is back-filled to its tenant's self facility, the only one there was.
   - `client_facility_moves` gains a **deferred constraint trigger refusing a COMMIT that leaves a move `in_progress`**, so "an in-progress row is visible only to the moving transaction" is enforced, not assumed.
   - `audit_logs.client_facility_id` survives `down` (append-only).
   - The tenant hard delete (D-23) now deletes the tenant's client facilities after its users.
   - A module shared by migrations (`facilityMigration.shared.ts`) may not add a column or create an index; `migrationScan` (AM-3, D-20) holds that, so the closed-world readers still see every addition.

**Why overriding Am. 2's rejection is right here.** Am. 2 rejected a database default for two reasons, and neither holds for the trigger as built:
- *"Invisible to memoryDb."* memoryDb enforces no NOT NULL either, so route tests see no difference. The service default, when P21-09 builds it, is what memoryDb will test.
- *"A silent re-ownership instead of a refusal."* For a child, the only value filled is the one the composite key would accept, and an explicit wrong value is still refused (23503). For a device, the self facility is filled only when it is the tenant's **only** facility, so nothing can be placed in the wrong client. Once a tenant has a second facility, a missing facility is a 23502 refusal, which is the "refusal, not re-ownership" Am. 2 asked for.

**Alternatives considered.**
| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Build P21-09's service default inside P20-07 | Out of the card's scope (the hooks and services are P21-09's). It touches every create path: the device, record, certificate, work order, IoT, attachment, NC, bulk import, scheduler and seed. It would also not cover raw-SQL writers (IoT ingestion, the ETL) |
| Model hooks (`beforeCreate` / `beforeBulkCreate`) that look the facility up | One extra query per create inside the hooks, which the query-count suites budget (P8-04). Raw-SQL inserts get no default. In memoryDb the lookup finds no self facility, so it would still need `allowNull: true` |
| Leave the column nullable until P21-09 | The ETL (P24-02) and every writer the hooks do not see would have no NOT NULL control, and the composite keys would not bind a NULL (MATCH SIMPLE). The database would prove nothing until a later release |
| Always fill the device's self facility, even in a multi-facility tenant | Silently places a client's device in the provider's own facility — the re-ownership Am. 2 rejected |

**Implications, including the bad ones.**
- **Once a tenant has a second facility, every create path that omits the facility fails with 23502 (a 500)** until P21-09's service default lands. No route creates a facility before P21-09, and the ETL writes facilities and devices explicitly, so nothing hits this today. But a facility inserted by hand or by a script into a live tenant breaks device creation there. This is recorded as a P21-09 hand-off.
- A forgotten facility in a **single-facility** tenant goes unnoticed. That is harmless, because there is only one facility, but it means the self-served path proves nothing about callers supplying the facility.
- A cross-tenant link is now refused at write time: a work order on another tenant's device (23503), or an attachment naming another tenant's record (23514/23503 at commit). Such legacy rows can only exist as the upgrade back-filled them. The orphan report's cross-tenant case is now a legacy-only case (the dbC fixture builds it that way). A database that already holds a work order, record, certificate or reading on another tenant's device **cannot be upgraded** until the row is repaired; the migration says so and records nothing.
- The model type `CreationOptional<ClientFacilityId>` reads as always set, while a row built in memory before insert may not carry it yet.
- The tenant hard delete is in practice refused for every tenant anyway: the self facility's CREATE audit row is a retained record. ADR-064's "a tenant that ever wrote an audit row is refused" was already the case for real tenants.

**`docs/` amended:** the P19-04 spec § 5.4 and § 6.3 (the default triggers, the nullable models, the as-built choices), each referencing this amendment.

---

## ADR-125: Device Types and Inspection Checklists Are One Global, Versioned Catalogue Without `tenant_id` — Written Only by the Platform Operator, a Published Version Is Immutable, Every Session Pins the Version It Used; Tenants Propose Through a Tenant-Scoped Table

**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted as the **TARGET — nothing here is built.** "One global, versioned catalogue, like `roles`" is the **owner's** decision (UD-3, 2026-10-07); the version model, the write path and the guards are decided by the ADR-writing agent under the owner's delegation · **Card:** P12-03 · **Builds in:** P19-01 (spec), P20-01/03, P21-01, P22-01, P24-02 (seeding) · **Works with:** ADR-064 §1 (global tables are guarded at the route), D-17 (`unscopedModels.d17`), D-05/P9-07 (`rawSqlTenantPredicate.d05`), ADR-124 (the facility dimension does not apply to global models), ADR-126 (sessions pin a version), ADR-127 (offline download) · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-upstream-adrs.md` · **Amended by:** Amendment 1 (P19-01, 2026-10-07, below § Status — the catalogue as specified); Amendment 2 (P20-01/03, 2026-10-07 — as built: the items keep DELETE for a draft, exact decimal strings, the as-built choices)

### Context

An IPM session is a checklist whose items depend on the device type: tools used, function checks, completeness, electrical-safety tests with limits, performance tests with a setting and a reference value (`docs/UPSTREAM/02-FEATURES.md` F-19 … F-22), plus sections common to every type (environment, supply, physical, maintenance tasks, recommendation — F-21). Upstream keeps 344 device types and ~480 checklist items in 12 `mst_*` tables and 5 `mapping_*` tables, writable only by seeders and SQL (drift D-10); a change to a mapping silently changes every past report, because reports are re-rendered from current rows.

The owner chose one catalogue for the whole platform rather than one per tenant (UD-3). Our data model admits a table without `tenant_id` only with a reason in an ADR (`docs/DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md`): roles, menus and the CMS are the precedents (ADR-064 §1, D-16), guarded by making every write route SUPERADMIN-only.

### Decision

1. **Global tables, no tenant column, no facility column** (ADR-124 does not apply):

   | Table | Holds |
   |---|---|
   | `device_types` | `name`, a normalised name (`UNIQUE lower(btrim(name)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`), `status` `active`/`retired`, `legacy_id` (04 § 4.3) |
   | `inspection_item_definitions` | the reusable item library (04 § 4.4): `section`, `label`, `input_kind` (`check`, `tri_state`, `condition_clean`, `measured`, `measured_with_limit`, `setting_measured_reference`, `text` — F-20), `unit`, `limit_op`/`limit_value`/`limit_unit`, `setting`, `reference_value`, `allowed_outcomes`, legacy keys |
   | `inspection_templates` | one per device type, plus exactly **one base template** (`device_type_id IS NULL`) holding the common sections of F-21 |
   | `inspection_template_versions` | `template_id`, `version_number` (`UNIQUE (template_id, version_number)`), `status` `draft`/`published`/`retired`, `base_version_id` (the base version materialised into it), `content_hash` (SHA-256 of the canonical item list), `change_note` (required to publish), `published_at/_by`, `retired_at/_by` |
   | `inspection_template_items` | the items **of one version**, copied from the library and frozen with it: section, label, input kind, unit, limits, setting, reference value, allowed outcomes, `required`, `sort_order`, `item_definition_id` (provenance, nullable) |

   04 § 4.5's `device_type_inspection_items` mapping is **replaced** by `inspection_template_items`: the version *is* the mapping. The ETL seeds version 1 of each type from the upstream `mapping_*` tables (P24-02).

2. **A version is self-contained and immutable once published.** Publishing materialises the current base version's items into the type version, computes `content_hash`, and in the same transaction moves the template's previously published version to `retired` — **exactly one published version per template** (partial unique index). After publish, a trigger refuses any `UPDATE` of a version's content columns and any `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` of its items, for every role (the 0057 pattern, tested as `callibrator_app`). Nothing in the catalogue is ever hard-deleted: a device type or a template is `retired`.

3. **Sessions pin a version.** `inspection_sessions.template_version_id` → `inspection_template_versions` RESTRICT, and each result pins `template_item_id` plus a snapshot of the label it showed (ADR-126). A report is rendered from the session's pinned version, so a later version never rewrites a past report (upstream's re-render defect). A **retired** version stays a valid definition: no new session may *start* on it online (409, "this checklist was replaced by version n; reload"), but a session captured offline against it is accepted (ADR-127 § 6).

4. **Who writes.** Every route that creates, edits, publishes or retires a catalogue row is `superAdminOnly`, held route by route by a new guard `inspectionCatalogueGlobal.guard` in the shape of `rolesGlobal.d16.test.js` (a new mutating route fails the inventory). Every publish and retire writes an audit row (PLATFORM tenant, like role changes) inside its transaction with the version id and content hash. No separation of duties is enforced between the operator who edits a draft and the one who publishes it (the platform has few operators; the same reason Q-54 left SoD open for single-admin tenants); a version built from a tenant's accepted proposal has two parties by construction.

5. **How a tenant asks for a change: `inspection_template_proposals` (tenant-scoped).** A provider's administrator proposes a new type, a new item or a changed limit in a row of **its own tenant** (`tenant_id`, scoped by the hooks; `status` `submitted`/`accepted`/`rejected`/`withdrawn`; the proposed items as JSON; reason). The operator reviews it (super-admin context) and, on acceptance, creates a draft version from it; the proposal records the resulting version id. Drafts never become visible to tenants, so no tenant ever sees another tenant's proposal or an unpublished change. On acceptance the operator removes anything that identifies a facility or person from the proposed text: catalogue text is platform content, readable by every tenant.

6. **Who reads.** Published and retired versions, their items, and active device types are readable by any authenticated principal holding `ipm`, `ipm-templates` or `equipment` read — facility-bound users included (ADR-124: global models have no facility dimension, and the route is facility-accessible). Drafts are operator-only. `GET /api/v1/ipm/templates/published` returns every published version with a strong `ETag` over the sorted `(version id, content_hash)` set and answers `304` to `If-None-Match` — the offline download of F-79/ADR-127.

7. **How the tenant hooks leave them alone, and the guards that change.**
   - The hooks scope a model if and only if it declares `tenantId`/`tenant_id` (`tenantScope.util.ts#tenantKeyOf`) — the mechanism `roles` already relies on. The five catalogue models declare neither (nor `clientFacilityId`), and must never declare an attribute of those names; the proposal model does, and is scoped.
   - `unscopedModels.d17`: the five models are added to `UNSCOPED` as group `"global"` with the reason "ADR-125: platform catalogue; writes superAdminOnly (inspectionCatalogueGlobal.guard)".
   - `rawSqlTenantPredicate.d05`: no change needed — it derives the tenant-scoped set from the real models, so catalogue tables are not in it. A raw statement that **joins** a tenant table to a catalogue table still binds the tenant (and, under ADR-124, the facility) predicate for the tenant table — the existing rule.
   - `twoTenantRoutes.guard`: catalogue read routes with a path parameter are allow-listed as `not-tenant-owned` (checked against the real model); mutating ones as `platform`. Proposal routes get `twoTenantSuite` tests asserting 404.
   - **No association from a catalogue model to a tenant model is declared** (`DeviceType.hasMany(CalibrationDevice)` and the like). A count of how many devices use a type is computed in the tenant's own context; a cross-tenant usage figure would be an aggregate of other tenants' data, and only the operator may see one.

### Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Per-tenant catalogues** (`tenant_id` on every catalogue table) | not the owner's choice; 118 copies of the same 344 types in the upstream case, and no shared improvement of a checklist |
| **Provider-owned catalogue referenced by facilities** | a cross-tenant foreign key (D-2) — only meaningful under the cross-tenant model ADR-124 rejected |
| **Mutable templates without versions** (upstream's model) | a changed limit rewrites every past report's meaning; fails ISO 17025 7.5 / Part 11 record integrity |
| **Version the item library instead of copying items into a version** | a version would then be a set of pointers into a moving library; the copy makes a version readable on its own, offline, forever |
| **Drafts stored in the global tables with a `proposed_by_tenant_id` column** | drafts would need an application-level visibility filter on a global table — "remember the WHERE"; a tenant-scoped proposal table gets the hooks for free |
| **Several published versions per type at once** (tenant picks) | that is per-tenant templates by another name; one published version keeps reports comparable |
| **Enforced four-eyes publishing** | blocks a platform with one operator; the immutable version, the audit row and the content hash make a bad publish visible and correctable by the next version |

### Implications, including the bad ones

- **A tenant cannot tailor a checklist.** A facility that needs an extra check adds an ad-hoc item in the session (F-39, F-42); a permanent change waits for the operator to publish. If tenants need their own templates, that is a new ADR.
- **The operator becomes the bottleneck** for catalogue quality and turnaround, and owns its content legally (it is platform content in compliance reports).
- **Publishing retires the previous version immediately**, so a technician online with a stale form gets a 409 and must reload; one offline keeps working (ADR-127).
- **Limit parsing** (`≤ 100 µA`, `± 10 %`) becomes structured data at seeding; values that do not parse are kept as text and evaluated by a person, not by the server (F-42).
- **Global text is readable by every tenant**: a careless change note or item label that names a facility leaks it platform-wide. The review in § 5 is a person, not a mechanism.
- **Five more unscoped models.** Each is a place where the deny-by-default hooks do nothing; the route guard is the only write control.

### Status

**Accepted 2026-10-07 as the target. Not built.** `docs/` amended as target: `DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md` (global tables), `UPSTREAM/04-SCHEMA-MAPPING.md` § 4.3–4.5, `UPSTREAM/02-FEATURES.md` F-20/F-22.

### ADR-125 Amendment 1 (2026-10-07, P19-01): the catalogue as specified — typed outcomes per section, structured limits with hard and soft ranges, no soft delete, `discarded` drafts, base rebase, the `calibration` read gate

**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted as the **TARGET — nothing here is built.** Decided by the P19-01 spec agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it); the seeded warn ranges and point 8 are flagged for the SME at UAT (P26-01) · **Card:** P19-01 · **Spec:** [`MEMORY/specs/P19-01-inspection-catalogue.md`](./specs/P19-01-inspection-catalogue.md) · **Record:** `MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-p19-01-domain-spec.md`

**Why an amendment.** Writing the spec against the code and the upstream views found that ADR-125 and `docs/UPSTREAM/04` were wrong or silent in ways that would have become defects. The spec's § 2 table G-1 … G-11 lists each; the decisions are:

1. **Outcome vocabulary per section (G-1).** `04` § 5 mapped the physical check and the consumable stock `1 / 0 / -1` to `pass / fail / not_applicable`; the upstream report prints them as *Baik / Cacat-Rusak Ringan / Rusak Berat* and *Iya / Tidak / Habis* (`app/Views/ipm/pdf_ipm.php`). `INSPECTION_OUTCOMES` therefore carries `pass, fail, not_applicable, done, not_done, good, minor_damage, major_damage, available, not_available, empty` (+ `INSPECTION_CLEANLINESS` `clean, dirty`), and a section registry in `@callibrator/contracts` fixes, per section, the allowed input kinds, the outcome set, whether ad-hoc rows are allowed and the print order.
2. **The read gate is `calibration` | `ipm` | `ipm-templates` (G-2)**, not `equipment`: `equipment` is the parent menu and gates only attachments; the device routes are gated by `calibration`.
3. **Structured limits (G-3).** An item's limit is `limit_op` (`lt, lte, gt, gte, between, plus_minus, plus_minus_pct, text`) with `limit_value`, `limit_low`/`limit_high`, `limit_nominal`, `limit_tolerance` and the verbatim `limit_text`; the nominal of a tolerance defaults to the item's numeric setting. Items also carry a **hard** input range (`valid_min/max`, 400 outside) and a **soft** plausibility range (`warn_min/max`, accepted and flagged). `applies_to_all_types` (upstream `flag`) is dropped: membership of the base template replaces it. One parser and one evaluator (`parseDecimal`, `parseLimit`, `normaliseUnit`, `evaluate`) live in `@callibrator/contracts` so the server, the offline client and the ETL cannot disagree; decimals are compared as scaled integers; there is no unit conversion (a limit whose unit differs from its item's is refused at publish).
4. **No soft delete in the catalogue (G-4).** The catalogue models are not `paranoid` and have no `defaultScope`: a `defaultScope` would make every include of a type or version an INNER JOIN (the A-75 trap) and hide sessions of retired types. `status` (`retired`) is the only removal; `device_types` name uniqueness covers every status. `DELETE`/`TRUNCATE` are refused by trigger on all catalogue tables and the application role has no `DELETE`.
5. **`calibration_devices.device_type_id` is RESTRICT (G-5)**, not `04`'s SET NULL.
6. **A draft can be `discarded` (G-6)** (terminal, rows kept); `version_number` is assigned at publish, so published numbers have no gaps. A published or retired version names exactly one publisher: a user, or a system actor from `SYSTEM_ACTORS` (`system:catalogue-seed`, `system:upstream-import`).
7. **Publishing a base version rebases every published type version in the same transaction (G-7)**: a new published version per typed template (its type items unchanged + the new base items, `rebased_from_version_id` set), the previous one retired. Open drafts are untouched. A session pins whatever it pinned.
8. **Template items always name their library definition (G-8)** (`item_definition_id` NOT NULL): the cross-version identity of a check. A one-off check during a visit is an ad-hoc *result* (P19-02), not a template item.
9. **Electrical-safety pass/fail is computed and not overridable** (re-measure instead); a performance item's pass/fail is the technician's, with the computed outcome kept beside it and a disagreement flagged. P19-02's result columns must carry `computed_outcome`, `outcome_source`, `warn_flag`, `cleanliness` and `raw_value`.
10. **The published catalogue document carries the active device types**, and its `ETag` covers them as well as the `(version id, content_hash)` set.
11. **Accepting a proposal copies nothing into the global tables**; it opens (or links) a draft, and the operator adds each item explicitly — the "strip identifying text" review is enforced by construction.
12. **No socket event and no webhook** for catalogue changes (clients learn through the `ETag` and the stale-version 409), and **no per-device-type IPM interval** (intervals are tenant policy, ADR-126 § 6).

**Alternatives considered:** keep `04`'s three-value mapping for every tri-state section (rejected: it records a heavily damaged device as "not applicable"); a single `limit_value` with ranges and tolerances left as text (rejected: the commonest upstream shape, "± N %", could never be evaluated); unit conversion between prefixes (rejected: a conversion table is a source of silent error at a safety limit; the form shows the unit); paranoid catalogue tables per convention (rejected: G-4); leaving type versions on the old base until each is republished by hand (rejected: the common sections would differ between types for an unbounded time); letting the technician override a computed electrical-safety fail (rejected: an objective limit; an override is a place for a wrong pass to hide); auto-copying accepted proposal items (rejected: tenant free text would reach every tenant without a deliberate act).

**Implications, including the bad ones:** every base change creates a new version of every typed template (~130 upstream) and gives every technician with an open form one stale-version 409; the outcome ENUM is wider and the renderer needs a label map per section; the ambiguous `N.NNN` decimal is read as a decimal point and relies on the on-screen confirmation (the ETL counts such values for the data-quality report); limits the parser cannot read (~25 % of the upstream performance references) are printed but never evaluated; the seeded warn ranges are a proposal until the SME confirms them.

**`docs/` amended (as target):** `UPSTREAM/04-SCHEMA-MAPPING.md` § 4.2 – 4.5, § 4.9, § 5; `UPSTREAM/02-FEATURES.md` F-20; `UPSTREAM/05-DATA-MIGRATION.md` § 3.1; `UPSTREAM/07-DATA-MINIMISATION.md` (catalogue rows); `DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md` (global tables); `TASKS/PHASE-12-UPSTREAM-DECISIONS-AND-ADRS.md` § 2 (the DoD's gate list).

### ADR-125 Amendment 2 (2026-10-07, P20-01 / P20-03): what building the catalogue's schema found — the items keep DELETE for a draft, the catalogue's decimals stay exact strings, and five smaller as-built choices

**Date:** 2026-10-07 · **Status:** Accepted and **BUILT** (migrations 0111, 0112). Decided by the P20-01/03 implementing agent under the owner's standing delegation (decide by best practice, record it) · **Cards:** P20-01, P20-03 · **Record:** [`MEMORY/records/2026-10-07-p20-01-03-catalogue-schema.md`](./records/2026-10-07-p20-01-03-catalogue-schema.md)

**Why an amendment (deviation protocol).** The P19-01 spec contradicted itself in one place and the codebase's own rules in another; each is resolved here rather than quietly in code.

1. **`inspection_template_items` keeps DELETE for the application role.** Spec § 7.7 says both "a draft's items are replaced wholesale" (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE allowed while the parent is a draft) and "`callibrator_app` has SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on all six tables and no DELETE"; Amendment 1 § 4 repeats the second. Both cannot hold: without DELETE the service cannot replace a draft's items as the application role. **Decision:** the five other tables (`device_types`, `inspection_item_definitions`, `inspection_templates`, `inspection_template_versions`, `inspection_template_proposals`) lose DELETE and TRUNCATE; the items lose TRUNCATE only, and their trigger `inspection_template_items_draft_only` refuses an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE whose parent version is not a draft — for every role, owner included (read under `FOR SHARE`, so a write racing a publish waits for it and is then refused). *Alternatives:* no DELETE and a draft edited by superseding drafts (every save a new version row — rejected: noise in the history and a revision counter that means nothing); soft-deleting draft items with a flag (rejected: a column every reader must remember, the `is_deleted` trap's shape). *Bad implication:* one more privilege the application role holds on a global table; the trigger is the only thing standing between it and a published version's items — proven as `callibrator_app` and as the owner (`inspectionCatalogue.p2003.live`).
2. **The catalogue's DECIMAL columns read back as exact strings, against D-21.** D-21 (`decimalGetters.d21`) gives every DECIMAL attribute a getter returning a JavaScript number. Spec § 6.1 carries limits as decimal strings and compares them on scaled integers ("0.1 + 0.2 problems do not exist at a limit boundary"), and the content hash (§ 7.6) is taken over the decimal text. **Decision:** the twenty limit/range attributes of `InspectionItemDefinition` and `InspectionTemplateItem` are a reviewed exception, held by `decimalGetters.d21` to read back as the string PostgreSQL returned. *Alternative:* the number getter (rejected: `0.7000001` rounds, `1e-7` prints with an exponent the canonical form refuses). *Bad implication:* code that adds two limits concatenates strings — the evaluator (P21-01, `evaluate`) is the only arithmetic allowed on them.
3. **`calibration_devices`' index is `(device_type_id, tenant_id)`**, not § 4.7's `(tenant_id, device_type_id)`: D-20 (`0067-foreign-key-and-tenant-indexes`) requires every foreign key to LEAD a non-partial index; the pair serves the per-tenant equality filter in either order.
4. **A published version's system publisher is checked by format in the database** (`^system:[a-z][a-z-]*$`), and by membership of the closed `SYSTEM_ACTORS` in the service: the ETL's actor (P24-02) then needs no migration. P20-03 adds `system:catalogue-seed` only.
5. **The seed's ids are fixed** (`5eedca7a-…`): every deployment's base version 1 is the same version with the same content hash (`165ac87a…bc89c`), and its APPROVE audit row is written once (a re-run after `down` finds it; `audit_logs` is append-only, so `down` leaves it).
6. **`canonicalTemplateVersion` sorts the items into read order itself** (section registry order, base before type, `sort_order`, id) instead of trusting the caller's order — two sides that fetched the rows differently still agree; moving an item changes its `sort_order` or section and therefore the text. Decimals are canonicalised (`80.0` and `80` hash alike).
7. **Down refuses** while the catalogue holds anything beyond the seed (0112) or any device type exists (0111): reverting would destroy catalogue rows, which ADR-125 never deletes.

**Deferred to P21-01 (with the API that uses them):** `parseDecimal`, `parseLimit`, `normaliseUnit`, `evaluate`, `resolveTemplateVersion`, `inspectionCatalogue.ts` request/response schemas, the validating constructors of the six brand ids, and the 400 on giving a device a retired type.

**`docs/` amended:** `MEMORY/specs/P19-01-inspection-catalogue.md` § 4.7, § 6.1, § 7.7 (pointers here); `docs/DATABASE/00-DATA-MODEL.md` (the catalogue tables as built).
